text:
sam: Hey team, POC with Acme hitting intermittent TCP resets to our private endpoint (NLB -> service). Streaming responses start then connection drops ~15-30s in. Any known causes on our side?

nisha: Do you have a curl -v or a packet capture? Could be proxy/firewall doing deep inspect.

sam: paste of curl -v: 
  * Connected to vpce-acme.example (10.0.2.15) port 443 (#0)
  * ALPN, offering h2
  * TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
  > GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
  < HTTP/2 200
  * Received 2.3k bytes, then:
  curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer

  No TLS alert printed by curl aside from the reset.

devon: I pulled a quick tcpdump from our side during repro: shows multiple packets, then a TCP RST from 10.8.4.12 -> 10.0.2.15 (src is customer egress). Looks like reset originates in their network.

andre: That aligns with a corporate firewall or TLS-intercepting proxy cutting session when it sees long-lived streaming or unexpected frames. Some proxies don't like HTTP/2 downstream streams and inject RST.

sam: Customer confirms they run a BlueCoat-like outbound proxy with TLS inspection and an extra stateful fw. They also have an outbound idle session timeout of 20s.

nisha: Two quick diagnostics for the customer to run (ask them to share outputs):
  1) openssl s_client -connect vpce-acme.example:443 -servername vpce-acme.example -alpn h2
  2) curl -v --no-buffer --http2 https://vpce-acme.example/v1/stream
  3) tcpdump on their egress: sudo tcpdump -n -w acme_dump.pcap host <their_ip> and port 443

devon: Also ask them to run the same curl but force HTTP/1.1 (curl --http1.1) to see if proxy chokes only on h2. If HTTP/1.1 stays up, it's definitely HTTP/2 handling.

andre: Workarounds while they triage:
  - Use a short polling endpoint instead of long-lived stream
  - Flip to HTTP/1.1 for the POC client
  - If they can, whitelist our endpoint IPs/SNI or bypass TLS inspect for that host
  - Longer-term: Dedicated reserved with static egress IPs so they can whitelist a single IP block (sales to confirm pricing/availability)

sam: They asked about Dedicated offering static egress — sales FYI, this is a blocker for them to move forward until networking is stable.

nisha: Security note: customer also requested certchain and whether we rotate client certs. Share only public chain and rotation cadence. Do NOT send private keys. security-bot: :lock:

devon: If they can provide PCAP + firewall logs showing the RST frames we can prove it originates on their side. After that we can recommend configuration changes or put in an engineering runbook for Private endpoints + corp proxies.

andre: Another angle: MTU/MSS clamping sometimes shows as mid-stream resets for big packets. Ask their network team if they're doing packet rewriting or TCP reset policies.

sam: I'll collect pcap and firewall logs and ask them to try --http1.1. Assigning devon to triage once we have files.

nisha: Also looping in sales for Dedicated/egress quote so customer has that option if they prefer to whitelist static IPs.

security-bot: Reminder: log any customer-sensitive data in secure ticket only (do not paste PCAPs to public channels).

sam: thanks all — I’ll update thread when I have the pcap + logs. :thumbsup:
